standard_prerequisites.use: They supply the maps $\Theta^p_{Y/X} : f_*\Omega^p_{Y/\mathbf{Z}} \to \Omega^p_{X/\mathbf{Z}}$ whose degree zero part is the trace, which are the components of the asserted map of complexes.

standard_prerequisites.name: The local presentation by universal finite syntomic families, smooth and etale over a dense open
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Discriminants, labels discriminant-lemma-locally-comes-from-universal-finite (invoked at proof line 4217), discriminant-lemma-universal-finite-syntomic-smooth (invoked at proof line 4282) and discriminant-lemma-universal-finite-syntomic-etale (invoked at proof line 4283)
standard_prerequisites.use: They present $f$ locally as a base change of a universal finite syntomic family $V_d \to U_d$ with $U_d$ smooth and $V_d \to U_d$ etale over a dense open, which is the situation in which the identities are checked.

core_obligations: Reduce to a local model: for $x \in X$ use the presentation of $f$ as a base change of a universal finite syntomic family $V_d \to U_d$, write $B = A \otimes_{A_d} B_d$ with $B_d = A_de_1 \oplus \ldots \oplus A_de_d$, and factor $U$ and $V$ through $U' = \mathbf{A}^N \times U_d$ and $V' = \mathbf{A}^N \times V_d$ so that any finite collection of forms on $U$ and $V$ is pulled back from the primed models; hence the identities $\mathrm{d}\Theta = \Theta\mathrm{d}$ and the Leibniz rule may be checked for $V' \to U'$ (proof lines 4216-4278).

Use that $U_d$ is smooth and $V_d \to U_d$ is etale over a dense open of $U_d$, so that the same holds for $V' \to U'$; since $\Omega^p_{U'/\mathbf{Z}}$ is torsion free it suffices to check the relations over that dense open, and after a surjective etale base change we may split the finite etale cover (proof lines 4280-4294).
In the split case $\coprod_{i=1,\ldots,d} W \to W$ with $W$ smooth over $\mathbf{Z}$, check the local properties directly, which finishes (1) and (2) (proof lines 4294-4299).

Deduce (3) from (2): relative differentials are the quotient of absolute differentials by the submodule generated by pullbacks of differentials of the base, so the Leibniz rule makes the map descend to a map of complexes over the base (proof lines 4301-4304).
proof_roadmap: Local model by universal families and the passage to $V' \to U'$ (proof lines 4216-4278).
Torsion freeness and reduction to the etale locus; splitting the cover (proof lines 4280-4294).
The split case and the end of (1) and (2) (proof lines 4294-4299).
(3) from (2) via the quotient description of relative differentials (proof lines 4301-4304).
difficulty_reason: The proposition assembles the individual Garel maps into a map of complexes from the pushforward of the de Rham complex of the source to the de Rham complex of the target, compatible with the trace in degree zero and with the Leibniz rule, and descending to relative differentials over a base (statement lines 4187-4213, with a reference environment recording Garel's paper). The proof reduces the identities to the local model given by the universal finite syntomic families, uses that the model is smooth with the morphism etale over a dense open and that the target differentials are torsion free to pass to a split finite etale cover, where the checks are immediate, and then derives the relative statement from the Leibniz rule. The two-stage reduction is the substance, so the claim is H2.
